The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\).

For each prime \(p\), write \(v_p(n)\) for the exponent of \(p\) in \(n\).  
When Mark replaces \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), the two exponent vectors are replaced by their coordinatewise minimum and maximum. Therefore, for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

A move changes the board exactly when the two numbers are not comparable by divisibility: if \(a\le b\) and \(a\nmid b\), writing \(a=gr,b=ge\) with \(r,s>1\), the new sum is \(g(1+rs)\), larger than the old sum \(g(r+s)\). Thus every changing move strictly increases the total sum of the board, while the product of all numbers remains invariant. Hence the process must end in a state where no move can change the board.

In that final state, every pair of numbers is comparable by divisibility. Sorting the final board as
\[
x_1\le x_2\le \cdots \le x_{2100},
\]
we must have
\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_{2100}.
\]
For each prime \(p\), the sequence \(v_p(x_1),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})\) is nondecreasing. Since the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents is invariant, this sequence must be the sorted list of the exponents of \(p\) among the numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\). So the final board is uniquely determined.

Now consider the 2026th smallest number, \(x_{2026}\). There are
\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]
numbers from \(x_{2026}\) to \(x_{2100}\). Thus for each prime \(p\), the exponent \(v_p(x_{2026})\) is the largest integer \(t\) such that at least \(75\) numbers from \(1\) to \(2100\) have \(v_p\ge t\).

The number of integers \(\le 2100\) divisible by \(p^t\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor.
\]
So we need
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor \ge 75.
\]
Since \(2100/75=28\), this is equivalent to
\[
p^t\le 28.
\]
Thus the exponent of \(p\) in \(x_{2026}\) is the largest power of \(p\) not exceeding \(28\). Therefore
\[
x_{2026}=\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,28).
\]

Now
\[
\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,28)
=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]
Its number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
